name: Krak des Chevaliers
ground: A spur in the Homs Gap, the one pass between the coast and the interior. The site is the whole strategy: hold this and you hold the road, and there is no second road.

keep.name: The inner keep
keep.note: Not a lone tower. The whole inner ring is the keep.

wards.name: Outer enceinte
wards.note: A complete ring. Taking it gains you a corridor and nothing else.

wards.name: Inner enceinte
wards.note: A second complete ring, higher, so the outer wall is overlooked from inside and an attacker who takes it is standing in a trap.

axis.name: The bent entry
axis.note: A hundred and thirty-seven metres of covered ramp that turns back on itself, so a ram can never build up a run at anything.

figures.value: about 2,000, which is why it could hold
a sloping stone skirt, so a mined wall collapses outward and buries the miners
1271, to a forged letter ordering surrender

lesson: The best-defended building of its century was never breached and was lost anyway, to a piece of paper. Concentric rings solve the problem of force completely and do nothing at all about the problem of authority — the garrison obeyed an order because orders were obeyed. Every choke point in a command tree has this exact shape: it is not the wall that fails.
